title: The Problem of Knowledge and Justification
text:
Epistemology is the branch of philosophy concerned with the nature, scope, and limits of knowledge. A central problem within this field is determining what constitutes sufficient justification for a belief to be considered true knowledge.

The traditional philosophical definition suggests that knowledge requires three conditions: truth (the belief must correspond to reality), belief (the individual must genuinely hold the belief), and justification (there must be adequate evidence or warrant supporting the claim). Justification theories range widely, encompassing rationalism—which posits that knowledge primarily comes from reason—and empiricism, which asserts that sensory experience is the main source of all knowledge.

The Gettier problem challenged the sufficiency of the traditional 'Justified True Belief' account. This challenge demonstrated scenarios where a belief could be logically justified and factually true, yet still seem to fail as genuine knowledge because the justification relied on accidental or false premises.
